title: Write down which source governs
statement: Write down which source governs a lesson, its own most specific named design over generic rules or a sibling lesson, and sort new feedback against it before acting.
detail: The reading project's QC checklist names its order of authority for when it and a source disagree: a dated ruling beats an undated principle, and a later ruling beats an earlier one (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`). Its criteria register puts a lesson's own design before the generic components document, the knowledge workbook and the procedure page, a rule promoted on 2026-08-25 after one lesson was built a tier too general (`grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, TOOL-01). A decision baseline written after a review proposed a large change of direction sorts incoming feedback into a demonstrated defect, a compatible refinement, a change of direction or insufficient evidence, holds any change of direction for one consolidated decision, and lets only an accepted amendment change the baseline and its tests (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-devfactory-2026-09-10/DECISION-BASELINE.md`). The analysis beside it says not to alternate between competing standards without recording which one governs (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-devfactory-2026-09-10/analysis-current-courses/VERIFICATION-PROPOSALS.md`). The governing design is cited exactly, by paragraph number.
against: Specificity is not the only rule of precedence: a later change-control baseline holds that recency, confidence and citation count do not supersede an earlier academic decision (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0218-devfactory-review-and-decision-brief-2026-09-10.qmd`, line 70). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-30-staging/contradictions.md`).
